title: Parabolic Positional Encoding: A Vision-Centric, Principled, Extrapolatable, and General Approach
claim: A simple, principled positional bias extrapolates beyond training resolution and generalizes across many datasets and modalities better than baselines.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, 3D surface then line plot then radar chart
description: Three rounded panels side by side, each with a bold caption underneath. Panel (a) shows a 3D parabolic surface, red at the top and blue at the edges, floating above an image patch with Δx and Δy arrows. Below it is the equation z = (a_x·Δx² + b_x·Δx) + (a_y·Δy² + b_y·Δy), captioned 'Parabolic Attention Bias'. Panel (b) is a line chart of accuracy against resolution, from 224² to 1024². The dashed red PaPE line stays highest and declines slowly, while the baselines (PaPE-RI, LookHere, nD-ALiBi, RoPE, RoPE-Mixed, nD-sincos) collapse earlier. Panel (c) is a radar chart over 8 datasets, with the dashed red PaPE polygon enclosing the outermost area. A shared color legend runs along the bottom. The eye goes first to the red surface and then to the dashed red PaPE curves.
caption: Parabolic Positional Encoding (PaPE). (a) PaPE encodes positions using an attention bias based on a sum of learnable parabolas with the relative position between tokens as the dependent variable. (b) PaPE has remarkable classification extrapolation, showing high robustness beyond the training resolution of 2242. (c) PaPE is a general vision positional encoding—on 8 datasets that span 4 vision modalities, PaPE matches the best baseline on 5 datasets and exceeds all on 2 datasets.
abstract: We propose Parabolic Positional Encoding (PaPE), a parabola-based positional encoding for vision modalities in attention-based architectures. Given a set of vision tokens-such as from videos, event camera streams, images, or point clouds-our objective is to encode their positions while accounting for the characteristics of vision modalities. Prior works have largely extended positional encodings from 1D-sequences in language to nD-structures in vision, but only with partial account of vision characteristics. We address this gap by designing PaPE from principles distilled from prior work: translation invariance, rotation invariance (PaPE-RI), distance decay, directionality, and context awareness. Extrapolation experiments on ImageNet-1K show how PaPE extrapolates remarkably well, improving in absolute terms by up to 10.5 over the next-best encoding. Generality experiments on 8 datasets across 4 modalities show that PaPE is a general vision positional encoding, as PaPE matches the best baseline on 5 datasets and exceeds all on 2 datasets. The code is available at https://github.com/DTU-PAS/parabolic-position-encoding.
